html:
The Sudanese revolution began on 19 December 2018 with protests over the tripled price of bread in Atbara and spread across Sudan, leading to the fall of Omar al-Bashir in April 2019.

Led by professional unions and neighbourhood resistance committees, protesters held a huge sit-in outside army headquarters in Khartoum from April 2019. Women were prominent, and a photo of a young woman in white leading chants became its symbol. The army removed Bashir on 11 April.

On 3 June, security forces, including the Rapid Support Forces, broke up the sit-in, killing over a hundred people. A deal in August 2019 set up a shared civilian and military government under Abdalla Hamdok, but the generals took full power in a coup in October 2021, leading to the war of 2023. It recalled the Arab Spring in Sudan.
sum: The Sudanese revolution began on 19 December 2018 with protests over the tripled price of bread in Atbara and spread across Sudan, leading to the fall of Omar al-Bashir in April 2019.
